title: Rosalind and the Orchard
premise: Mara Quintana returns to her grandfather's crumbling lighthouse on the coast of Aldermoor to help pack up the house before it's sold, dreading the family reunion where everyone will ask why she still hasn't published the novel she's been 'about to finish' for ten years. To survive the weekend, she recruits Elias Wren, the quiet orchardist who tends the abandoned apple trees behind the lighthouse, to pose as her boyfriend — an arrangement that curdles into something real by dessert. As the sale deadline looms, Mara must choose between the containable life she's rehearsed in fiction and the untrainable heart standing in the orchard; she finally says the sentence she has practiced for a decade — that she never left because leaving was easier than being seen — and chooses to stay, buying back the orchard land with her first advance.
about_author: Isandro Dunmore is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who spent six seasons on the North Atlantic coast before turning to writing full-time. He lives in a converted boathouse with two indifferent cats and an orchard he refuses to prune properly.

chapters.title: The Letter from the Trust
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. A solicitor's letter announces the lighthouse will be sold in eight weeks unless family claims otherwise. Mara packs her unfinished manuscript and takes the train north, telling herself this is logistics, not homecoming. Emotional beat: dread disguised as efficiency.

chapters.title: Salt in the Walls
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. She arrives at the shuttered lighthouse, finds her grandfather's old logbooks, and feels the past press in. The reunion invitations sit on the table, already addressed. Emotional beat: grief arriving ahead of schedule.

chapters.title: The Man Among the Trees
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Elias tends the feral orchard behind the lighthouse at dawn, grafting scions onto trees nobody owns. He notices a light in the keeper's cottage for the first time in years. Emotional beat: cautious curiosity.

chapters.title: Apples as Collateral
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Mara catches Elias picking apples on 'her' property and marches out to confront him; he offers her a basket instead of an argument. They bicker about ownership of things neither can keep. Emotional beat: sparks through friction.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Almost
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Flashback woven in: the sentence she rehearsed at nineteen, the night she almost told her family she wanted to write instead of take over the family marine supply business — and fled to the city instead. Emotional beat: shame as muscle memory.

chapters.title: The Reunion Looms
chapters.summary: Aunt Beatrice calls with a headcount; Mara's cousin Priya is bringing her perfect fiancé. Mara lies before she can stop herself: she's bringing someone too. Emotional beat: panic crystallizing into a plan.

chapters.title: An Indecent Proposal, Politely Worded
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. She finds Elias at the orchard fence and asks him to be her fake boyfriend for the reunion weekend. He laughs, then studies her too carefully, then says yes — for a price: she helps him save the orchard from the sale. Emotional beat: bargain struck, trap set.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Elias drafts absurd 'rules' over cider: no real feelings, no questions about his past, hand-holding permitted only under observation. Mara signs with a flourish. Both know rules are made to be broken. Emotional beat: playful denial.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner for Two
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. They practice their story on the lighthouse gallery — how they met (the orchard), first date (rain, a ferry delay). The invented details feel dangerously like memories. Emotional beat: intimacy by rehearsal.

chapters.title: The Orchard at Night
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. A storm knocks down the oldest tree; Mara appears with rope and tarps without being asked. Working side by side until midnight, they talk around their wounds. Emotional beat: first crack in the armor.

chapters.title: Arrival of the Quintanas
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. The family descends on the harbor inn. Her mother's appraisal of Elias is surgical; her father's silence is louder. Mara performs happiness like a second language. Emotional beat: performance under pressure.

chapters.title: Dessert Is Served
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. At the reunion dinner, Elias defends Mara's unpublished novel against a cousin's mockery with unexpected ferocity. Under the table, his hand finds hers — not per the rules. Emotional beat: the fake becomes felt.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Logbook
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Reading her grandfather's final entries, Mara learns he secretly kept every rejection letter her manuscript ever received, annotated with pride. Emotional beat: posthumous permission to want things.

chapters.title: What Elias Isn't Saying
chapters.summary: Priya, POV. Sharp-eyed Priya corners Elias at breakfast and pokes holes in the couple's story — then, surprisingly, offers to keep the secret if he makes it true. Emotional beat: the audience sees what the leads won't.

chapters.title: The Ferry Delay
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Stranded overnight by fog after a family errand, Mara and Elias share a hotel room with one bed, naturally. Nothing happens except everything: conversation until 3 a.m., her head on his shoulder. Emotional beat: tenderness without permission.

chapters.title: Rules, Broken
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Back at the cottage, Mara realizes she's stopped writing the novel and started living its plot. She tries to reassert distance and fails within a day. Emotional beat: the heart outpacing the contract.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. A property developer visits the orchard with plans for a resort, offering Elias a caretaker job if he stops contesting the sale. Temptation wears a nice suit. Emotional beat: stakes sharpened.

chapters.title: First Kiss, Worst Timing
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. After Elias turns the developer down, adrenaline and relief tip them into a kiss in the rain-soaked orchard. Mara pulls away, terrified, and invokes Rule One. Emotional beat: joy followed immediately by retreat.

chapters.title: The Cold War of Small Gestures
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Days of pointed politeness: he fixes her porch step, she leaves cider on his fence post. Neither apologizes; both ache. Emotional beat: longing expressed through labor.

chapters.title: Beatrice Knows
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Aunt Beatrice reveals she knew the relationship was staged from minute one — and that she staged nothing, because she saw how Elias looked at Mara before any deal existed. Emotional beat: the mask declared unnecessary.

chapters.title: The Manuscript Problem
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Mara rereads her decade-old draft and finds it bloodless — a novel about a woman who never risks anything. She begins rewriting herself into it. Emotional beat: art catching up to life.

chapters.title: Elias's History
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. His backstory surfaces: he once inherited a family farm and sold it under pressure, and has spent years tending other people's land because he couldn't face his own failure. Emotional beat: mirror revealed.

chapters.title: The Auction Notice
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. The trust moves the auction up three weeks. The orchard parcel is listed separately — Elias can't afford it. Mara calculates what her savings could do and doesn't tell him. Emotional beat: secret generosity forming.

chapters.title: Family Dinner, Round Two
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. A tense supper where Mara's father finally speaks: he never wanted her to abandon writing; he assumed she had. Ten years of misread silence collapse. Emotional beat: misunderstanding dismantled.

chapters.title: Almost the Sentence
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. On the gallery at sunset, Mara starts to say the rehearsed sentence — and Elias, sensing confession coming, stops her mouth with a kiss, afraid of what truth ends. Emotional beat: interruption as self-protection.

chapters.title: The Betrayal
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Elias discovers Mara's bid paperwork for the orchard — she planned to buy it without telling him, the way everyone important always decides for him. He walks out. Emotional beat: kindness experienced as control.

chapters.title: Empty Orchard
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Three days of silence. Mara writes furiously, finishes the novel at 4 a.m., and understands the ending only now that she's lost the man. Emotional beat: grief converted to craft.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Auction day at the harbor hall. Bidding war over the orchard parcel between the developer and an anonymous phone bidder. Emotional beat: public spectacle, private stakes.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Bidder
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. The winning bid is Mara's — placed through her agent using her just-sold novel's advance. She stands to claim it and finds the hall emptying, Elias gone. Emotional beat: victory hollowed out.

chapters.title: What the Trees Saw
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Elias walks the coast road toward the ferry, passing the orchard one last time. Each tree holds a memory of her. He sits down among them and cannot leave. Emotional beat: belonging outweighing pride.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Mara finds him in the orchard at dusk and finally says the sentence she rehearsed for a decade: 'I left because staying meant you'd all see me fail — and I'd rather disappear than be known.' Then adds the new one: 'I'm done disappearing.' Emotional beat: climax, catharsis.

chapters.title: Grafting
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Elias answers not with words but with work: he shows her how to graft a new scion onto the storm-broken tree — two varieties, one trunk. Emotional beat: forgiveness as horticulture.

chapters.title: Reading the Rejections Aloud
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Mara reads her grandfather's annotated rejection letters to Elias by lamplight, laughing at his marginalia ('fools,' 'their loss,' 'keep going'). Emotional beat: legacy reclaimed as comedy.

chapters.title: The Family Returns
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The Quintanas arrive to help restore the lighthouse; Priya smugly collects on her bet with Elias; even the father picks apples badly and happily. Emotional beat: found place, found people.

chapters.title: Proofs Arrive
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Advance copies of her novel arrive — titled 'The Orchard Keeper.' She inscribes the first copy to Elias and hides it in the cider press for him to find. Emotional beat: shyness transformed into declaration.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Relit
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. With the town's help, they restore the lamp room; the light turns for the first time in nine years, visible from the orchard ridge. Emotional beat: continuity restored, symbol earned.

chapters.title: Contract Renewed
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Mara burns the original fake-dating rules in the woodstove and hands Elias a single new page: no expiration date. He signs. Emotional beat: playful callback turned vow.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The town's first harvest festival in the revived orchard; cider, dancing, Beatrice orchestrating romance like weather. Mara reads the opening page of her next book aloud. Emotional beat: communal joy.

chapters.title: Winter Scion
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. First frost. Elias plants the grafted sapling where the old tree fell and proposes — not with a ring but with deed papers adding Mara's name to the orchard. She says yes before he finishes. Emotional beat: rootedness chosen.

chapters.title: Rosalind and the Orchard
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Epilogue, spring: blossoms over the headland, the lighthouse beam sweeping at dusk, Mara writing at the kitchen window while Elias prunes. The last line mirrors the first sentence of her novel. Emotional beat: love and duty reconciled; belonging complete.
